title: Why normalize?
text: Divide an embedding by its L2 norm to make its length one. The dot product of two unit vectors equals their cosine similarity.
credit: Passage written for this course

title: The CLIP training loss
text: CLIP compares each image with every caption in a batch. Row and column softmaxes form two distributions. The loss averages the negative log probabilities of the observed image-caption partners.
credit: Passage written for this course

title: Retrieval and generation
text: An embedding model finds relevant source passages. A separate generative model can use those passages to write an answer. A high retrieval score is not a guarantee that the passage answers the question.
credit: Passage written for this course

title: The text readout in original CLIP
text: Original CLIP uses causal self-attention in its text Transformer. The end-of-text token can attend to the whole preceding description. Its final state provides the text representation.
credit: Passage written for this course

title: Shorter vectors
text: With Matryoshka embeddings, keep the first 512, 256, or 128 coordinates, then normalize again. Shorter vectors save index memory. Multimodal retrieval at 128 dimensions can lose quality.
credit: Passage written for this course

title: Solar power
text: Photovoltaic panels convert sunlight into electrical energy. Solar farms arrange many panels in rows. Power production varies with sunlight and cloud cover.
credit: Passage written for this course
